prerequisites: Kinematics and dynamics of the material point.
Theory of linear differential equations, with constant coefficients, of the first and second order, homogeneous and non-homogeneous.

learning_outcomes.text: The course provides students with knowledge regarding the kinematics and dynamics of machines and mechanical devices and systems.
The objective is to enable students to understand and approach the study and functional design of machines and mechanical systems.
The course allows the student to apply kinematic and dynamic knowledge to machines and mechanical systems, to machines in open kinematic chain, and to planar robotic systems.
It also allows evaluating the nominal characteristics of the mechanical devices constituting the machine and the energy performance of machines and mechanical devices.
Have the ability to collect and interpret data deemed useful for the study of the performance of mechanical devices and systems.
Be able to communicate information and solutions through numerical elaborations regarding the functional characteristics of the machine.
Have the ability to integrate the knowledge acquired in the course with that of the disciplines of Mechanical Design and Science of Constructions and other characteristic teachings.

syllabus_topics: KINEMATICS AND DYNAMICS OF PLANAR MECHANISMS (4 CFU): Kinematics and dynamics of planar mechanisms. Mechanisms for automatic machines. Articulated systems in open kinematic chain. Analytical kinematics.
ADHESION AND FRICTION (1 CFU): Adhesion and sliding friction. Rolling friction. Rolling bearings. Longitudinal vehicle dynamics.
BRAKES AND CLUTCHES (1 CFU): Shoe brakes, drum brakes, disc brakes. Planar, conical, and centrifugal clutches.
MOTION TRANSMISSION BY FLEXIBLE ELEMENTS (1 CFU). Fundamental equation. Forcing. Transmission ratio. Efficiency. Optimal speed.
GEARS AND GEAR TRAINS (2 CFU): Cylindrical, helical, bevel gears. Ordinary and epicyclic gear trains.
MOTOR-LOAD COUPLING (1 CFU): Motor-load coupling: direct, with speed reducer, with friction clutch. Machine efficiency.
MECHANICS OF VIBRATIONS (2 CFU): Free and forced vibrations of single-degree-of-freedom systems. Vibrations due to constraint oscillation and rotating eccentric mass. Vibration isolation.
assessment_rules: The assessment aims to evaluate both the ability to solve numerical exercises (written test) and the ability to present theoretical concepts (oral interview). The written test, typically lasting 3 hours, covers types of exercises performed in class and requires solving kinematics and dynamics problems related to planar mechanisms, friction systems, belt transmissions, gear trains, motor-load couplings, and single-degree-of-freedom vibrating systems. The oral interview, lasting 20-30 minutes, covers topics discussed in class and is accessible after passing the written test with a minimum score of 18/30. The final grade is the average of the two tests and must be above 18/30 (rounded up). Minimum learning requirements include conceptually correct problem-solving in the written test (not neglecting any of the three exercises) and sufficient mastery, language proficiency, and autonomous elaboration of concepts in the oral test (not being completely unaware of any requested topic).
